findings.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 — P2, anchor 100: The raw-query conversion leaves the org and team authorization branches unverified against PostgreSQL because `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`((\"teamId\" = ${testData.team.id}) AND (\"isTeamBooking\" = true)) OR ...\`)` only compares Prisma.Sql objects, so malformed SQL or parameter serialization in those production scopes reaches users without a passing-query acceptance test.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:203 — P2, anchor 100: The denial-path conversion lacks an execution test because `expect(conditions).toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION)` never runs the `1=0` fragment through `$queryRaw`, so a non-owner or invalid-options request can fail at query time instead of reliably returning no bookings.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:294 — [75/P2] The team raw-query path has no execution assertion because `const conditions = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();` is followed only by `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`, so a PostgreSQL-incompatible array binding or predicate is green in CI and fails when a team-scoped Insights query runs.

packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:330 — [75/P2] The org raw-query path has no execution assertion because `const conditions = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();` is followed only by `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`, so a PostgreSQL-incompatible array binding or predicate is green in CI and fails when an organization-scoped Insights query runs.

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:295 — P2, anchor 100: The raw-query conversion leaves the org and team authorization branches unverified against PostgreSQL because `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`((\"teamId\" = ${testData.team.id}) AND (\"isTeamBooking\" = true)) OR ...\`)` only compares Prisma.Sql objects, so malformed SQL or parameter serialization in those production scopes reaches users without a passing-query acceptance test.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the tests compare Prisma.Sql objects using toEqual() rather than actually executing the generated SQL against the database. Looking at the diff, the test at line 295 (and similar tests) changed from comparing Prisma object structures to comparing Prisma.sql template literals. While there is one test ('should combine authorization and filter conditions') that does execute the SQL via prisma.$queryRaw, the specific org and team authorization branches (buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, buildTeamAuthorizationCondition) are only tested by comparing the Prisma.Sql objects, not by executing them. This is a valid concern about test coverage - if the SQL syntax is malformed, these tests would still pass because they only compare the Prisma.Sql object structure, not the actual query execution. This is an important non-bug issue about incomplete test coverage for the new raw SQL approach.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:203 — P2, anchor 100: The denial-path conversion lacks an execution test because `expect(conditions).toEqual(NOTHING_CONDITION)` never runs the `1=0` fragment through `$queryRaw`, so a non-owner or invalid-options request can fail at query time instead of reliably returning no bookings.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the tests for NOTHING_CONDITION (lines 207, 242) only check that the condition equals `Prisma.sql`1=0`` but never actually execute this SQL fragment through `$queryRaw`. While the diff does show one test (around line 477-487) that executes `getBaseConditions()` through `$queryRaw`, the denial-path tests (non-owner, invalid options) don't verify the SQL actually works at runtime. This is a valid test coverage concern - the `1=0` SQL fragment could theoretically fail in certain database contexts, and the tests don't verify it executes correctly. However, this is a test completeness issue rather than a bug, as `1=0` is standard SQL that should work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:294 — [75/P2] The team raw-query path has no execution assertion because `const conditions = await service.getAuthorizationConditions();` is followed only by `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql\`...\`)`, so a PostgreSQL-incompatible array binding or predicate is green in CI and fails when a team-scoped Insights query runs.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the team-scoped test at line 292 only asserts that the SQL template matches expected structure via toEqual(), but doesn't actually execute the generated SQL against PostgreSQL to verify it's valid. Looking at the diff, the test 'should return team conditions for team scope' creates conditions and only checks they match a Prisma.sql template. In contrast, the 'getBaseConditions' test at line 477 actually executes the SQL with prisma.$queryRaw. This is a legitimate test coverage gap - the team authorization path generates raw SQL with array bindings (ANY(${[...]})) that could fail at runtime if the SQL syntax is incorrect, but CI would pass because only the template structure is verified. This is a valid concern about incomplete test coverage for the new raw SQL approach.
